data.title: SAP Stock (SAP) Gains on Reports of AI Efficiency Push
data.description:
The stock of German software giant SAP (SAP) is up about 3% on Nov. 27 on reports that the company is planning to cut as many as 10,000 jobs as it adopts and uses more artificial intelligence (AI) technologies.

Media reports say that SAP is reshaping its software business for the AI era and plans to scale back its human workforce as a result. "The business environment in which we operate is changing rapidly through A.I., and we are continuously reviewing how our organization and workforce need to evolve to remain successful," said SAP in a written statement.

Above is a chart from TipRanks that shows the three-month performance of SAP stock. As one can see, the company's share price has declined 5% in the last 12 weeks.

AI Job Losses

Other software companies have also cut their workforces this year due to growing adoption of AI, which can perform many of the coding tasks of software engineers. Atlassian (TEAM) said in March it would cut about 1,600 jobs to fund further AI investments, while Cloudflare (NET) said in May that it was eliminating 1,100 roles as it adopts an "AI-first operating model."

Microsoft (MSFT) has been most aggressive, eliminating about 4,800 positions, or 2% of its global workforce, this year and offering voluntary buyouts to 60,000 other employees. In the U.S., employers have cited AI as a major reason for more than 120,000 job cuts through October of this year, according to outplacement firm Challenger, Gray & Christmas.

SAP's Workforce

SAP currently employs more than 110,000 people worldwide. All departments at the company have been asked to identify potential cuts, with engineering a particular focus, according to a report by Reuters. The German tech giant last cut jobs in 2024, when it eliminated about 10,000 positions through a voluntary departure program.

The latest reports of job cuts come after SAP completed four acquisitions this year: Reltio, Dremio, Prior Labs and TechWolf. The acquisitions are intended to help SAP organize company data, develop AI models for business information, and analyze workforce skills.

Is SAP Stock a Buy?

TipRanks data shows that analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on SAP stock. This is based on seven Buys and one Hold assigned in the past three months. The average SAP price target of $270.07 per share implies 29% upside potential from current levels.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: 'Time to Rethink,' Says Investor About Sandisk Stock
data.description:
Nobody would accuse Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) of having a quiet fall. AI data centers are still driving record sales and profits at the flash memory maker, but the outlook for its chips has darkened quickly. Industry trackers now expect flash prices to fall next year, Chinese cloud companies are buying less storage, and a Chinese competitor is winning market share. Investors have responded by selling hard.

Today, the stock, along with a plethora of beaten-down tech names, is surging in the shortened Black Friday trading session, after it more than halved over the past month. The stock is now selling about 72% below its June 25 record close, adjusted for the 8-for-1 split that took effect last week.

So, obviously, for the most part, bears have been in control here recently, after the stock was the name to own in the first half of the year.

For investor Louis Gerard, the worries behind the selloff are real. TrendForce has cut its forecast for fourth-quarter NAND contract price gains and now expects prices to slip early next year. Chinese cloud providers have also reduced their 2027 enterprise SSD orders by more than U.S. buyers are adding, while global bit supply is set to grow 25% to 30%. Meanwhile, China's YMTC shipped more NAND than Sandisk in the second quarter, according to Counterpoint.

The company's own numbers point to slower growth. Fiscal Q1 revenue jumped 378% year over year to $11.03 billion and beat estimates. But Q2 guidance implies about 12% sequential growth, half the previous quarter's pace, because management expects only modest price increases.

Still, Gerard thinks the share price now reflects most of that. Sandisk trades at less than 5x trailing non-GAAP earnings, which makes it one of the cheapest names in the semiconductor sector. Its free cash flow over the past 12 months equals about 21% of its market cap, and it generated $5.7 billion in fiscal Q1 alone.

The business also has more visibility than a typical memory maker. Long-term contracts with eight customers cover about half of Sandisk's fiscal 2027 bits and two-thirds of fiscal 2028's, with $88.9 billion in remaining performance obligations. Those contracts include price floors, although Gerard notes they have never been tested in a real downturn, and customers will have every reason to push for better terms if spot prices fall far below what they agreed to pay.

Still, the outlook might also turn out less grim than feared. Sandisk expects NAND bit demand to grow about 40% in 2027, well above TrendForce's supply forecast. If enterprise demand holds up and the contract floors do their job, Gerard thinks current Wall Street estimates for fiscal 2028 could prove right, leaving plenty of room for the stock to recover.

The investor still sees cracks in the story, which keeps him from turning bullish. But at these levels, he can no longer justify a bearish stance.

Hence, Gerard has upgraded SNDK's rating from Sell to Hold (i.e., Neutral). (To watch Gerard's track record, click here)

Three Street analysts are also on the sidelines here, but with an additional 12 Buys, the stock claims a Strong Buy consensus view. Going by the $252.10 average price target, a year from now, shares will be changing hands for a 205% premium. (See SNDK stock forecast)

data.title: SanDisk (SNDK) Soars to Lead a Rally in Memory and Storage Stocks on Black Friday
data.description:
Shares of NAND flash memory maker SanDisk (SNDK) rose as high as 14% to about $84 on Black Friday morning. This followed a selloff in memory and storage stocks earlier in the week. This came after enthusiasm surrounding Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia's (NVDA) CEO faded. data.title: 'The Time Has Come,' Says Top Investor About Rocket Lab Stock
data.description:
Rocket Lab (NASDAQ:RKLB) has spent much of 2026 operating in reverse. In the spring, its shares soared on record first-quarter results, a round of analyst upgrades and a wave of excitement about space stocks as SpaceX's IPO drew closer. The stock has since given back nearly all of those gains. Some of the slide came as SpaceX went public in June, and more of it came as Neutron, Rocket Lab's medium-lift reusable rocket that hasn't flown yet, slipped into next year. Mizuho added to the gloom earlier this week, when it started covering the stock with an Underperform (i.e., Sell) rating. By Wednesday morning, the shares had sunk to a level not seen since early December 2025.

The stock is up in today's shortened Black Friday session, but is still roughly two-thirds below its record close of $150.23 on May 27.

Investor Daniel Sparks, who contributes to The Motley Fool and ranks among the top 3% of investors on TipRanks, thinks the more telling story is what the business did while the stock went around in a circle. Rocket Lab brought in about $882 million in revenue over the past four quarters, roughly 59% more than in the 12 months to September 2025. Growth has also picked up. Third-quarter sales jumped 73% year over year to a record $268 million, and fourth-quarter guidance implies about 56% YoY growth at the midpoint. Rocket Lab has issued plenty of new stock, partly to help fund its pending Iridium Communications deal, but the investor points out that sales have grown much faster than the share count.

At around $50, Rocket Lab has a market cap of roughly $32 billion, or about 36 times trailing 12-month sales. Sparks calls that a rich price for a company that still loses money, and he argues that a good chunk of it is riding on Neutron.

That is where he gets cautious. Rocket Lab has 16 Neutron missions lined up, and it signed eight of them in the third quarter for more than $515 million. Most of the new deals are for flights years away. ICEYE's three launches start in late 2028, and Muon Space and Starcloud are booked for 2029 and beyond. Only about a third of the company's $3.6 billion backlog is expected to become revenue over the next 12 months, and Sparks believes the long-dated Neutron work is a large slice of what's left. The rocket's debut is penciled in for 2027, but no date has been set while the first-stage tank goes through assembly and testing.

The early flights may not pay off either. Rocket Lab has already recorded a forward loss reserve against Neutron's second flight. In other words, it expects that launch to cost more than the customer is paying for it, and it has booked the loss in advance. Adjusted EBITDA showed an $18 million loss in Q3, and the company guides for another loss of $14 million to $20 million in Q4. CFO Adam Spice told analysts he expects adjusted EBITDA to turn positive no more than six months after Neutron first flies successfully.

Sparks doesn't play down the risks. Neutron has yet to leave the ground, and a steady launch schedule is a separate hurdle after that. A stock this volatile could also lurch hard in either direction. Still, revenue is racing ahead of the share count and Neutron's order book keeps filling, so he sees a case for patient investors. The 5-star investor would build a position through several smaller purchases rather than one lump sum. (To watch Sparks' track record, click here)

On the Street, RKLB stock claims a Moderate Buy consensus view, a rating based on 15 Buys, 3 Holds and 1 Sell. At $92.33, the average price target implies shares will gain 86% in the months ahead. (See RKLB stock forecast)

data.title: Bitcoin (BTC) Heads for First Weekly Gain in Nearly Two Months
data.description:
Bitcoin (BTC) was rising in early trading on Nov. 27 and on track to end a seven-week losing streak. The largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization was trading as high as $61,500 heading into the weekend and pacing for a 0.50% increase over the last five trading sessions, according to data from TipRanks.

While modest, the weekly gain would be the first one for Bitcoin in nearly two months as cryptocurrencies have come under relentless selling pressure. Bitcoin's current seven-week losing streak is the second-longest downturn for the digital asset on record.

A Month to Forget for Bitcoin

Heading into the end of November, BTC is down 20% on the month, its biggest monthly decline since June of this year. The price of Bitcoin fell to just under $56,000 on Nov. 21, its lowest level in two years. BTC is trending higher to end a volatile trading week with U.S. markets open for a shortened trading session on Nov. 27, a day after markets were closed for Thanksgiving.

U.S. stocks, particularly technology names, are surging to end the week as investors look to buy the dip in beaten down names such as Nvidia (NVDA) and CoreWeave (CRWV). Precious metals are also getting a bounce, with silver's price up 9% and gold adding 3% on the day. Year-to-date, Bitcoin has declined 30%, data from TipRanks shows.

Bitcoin ETF Outflows

Outflows from Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have reached a record $4.71 billion during November and are on track to surpass $5 billion by month's end, according to Farside Investors data. The previous monthly record for Bitcoin ETF withdrawals was set in June of this year, when outflows reached $4.50 billion.

BlackRock's (BLK) iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) has accounted for the most outflows this month. The redemptions from spot ETFs are accelerating as Bitcoin's price struggles to remain above the key support level of $60,000. Institutional investors have aggressively sold out of the ETFs since a $6.3 billion theft was reported at the Binance crypto exchange on Oct. 29.

BTC Price Action

Below is a chart from TipRanks that looks at the price movements of Bitcoin over the past three months. As one can see, the price of BTC is down 24% in the last 12 weeks.

data.title: Why Is MercadoLibre (MELI) Stock Up 4% Today, 11/27/26?
data.description:
MercadoLibre (MELI) stock is up about 4% on Friday as Brazilian markets rally following the appointment of veteran banker Luiz Carlos Trabuco as the country's next finance minister. The stock is also getting attention as MercadoLibre and Amazon (AMZN) compete for shoppers during Brazil's Black Friday shopping event.

Trabuco is the chairman of Bradesco, Brazil's second-largest private bank. He previously served as its CEO from 2009 to 2018 and has decades of experience in the country's financial sector. His appointment by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is being viewed as a market-friendly choice that could help restore investor confidence.

Investors see Trabuco as a more business-oriented leader who could improve confidence in Brazil's economy. Brazil's benchmark Ibovespa index jumped about 6% on Thursday as news of his appointment circulated, while the Brazilian real also strengthened against the U.S. dollar.

MercadoLibre Faces Amazon in Black Friday Battle

Meanwhile, MercadoLibre is gearing up for Black Friday in Brazil, where it faces competition from Amazon and other e-commerce platforms. The company has committed more than 100 million reais in coupons and plans to feature 37 million discounted product listings during its biggest promotional campaign to date. It is also offering more installment payment options through Mercado Pago.

The shopping event is important for MercadoLibre because Brazil is one of its largest markets. Strong Black Friday sales could help drive higher e-commerce activity and increase the use of Mercado Pago. However, the company is also competing with Amazon on discounts and payment offers, which could put pressure on margins. The results of the shopping event could give investors a better indication of how well MercadoLibre is holding up against Amazon as competition in Brazil's e-commerce market intensifies.

Should You Buy MELI Stock?

Wall Street believes that MELI stock should be priced significantly higher. During the past three months, analysts have issued an average MELI price target of $2,142, implying upside of 40.89% from current prices. The highest price target sits at $2,600, while the lowest is at $1,600. Of the 12 analysts covering MELI, 10 rate it a Buy, two rate it a Hold, and none rate it a Sell.

data.title: Imperial Brands Stock (IMB) Jumps 15% on Takeover Rumors
data.description:
The stock of British tobacco giant Imperial Brands ($GB: IMB) is up 15% after rumors of a takeover surfaced. The Financial Times has reported that Altria Group (MO) is exploring a $30 billion acquisition of Imperial Brands, a key rival in the tobacco space.

U.S.-based Altria, which makes Marlboro cigarettes, is considering an all-cash offer for British rival Imperial Brands but is also in discussions with a third party about breaking up Imperial to mitigate antitrust concerns around a potential deal. Imperial Brands, which makes Winston cigarettes, is currently valued at $30 billion based on its market capitalization.

A Japan Tobacco Partnership

Bloomberg is reporting that Japan Tobacco (JP:2914) could be a potential partner of Altria on the purchase of Imperial Brands. Altria has not publicly announced an acquisition. The media reports say that the tobacco company's board of directors is exploring its options.

Under takeover rules in the U.K., Altria, and possibly Japan Tobacco, have until Dec. 24 of this year to make an acquisition offer for Imperial Brands or announce that it will not proceed, unless the deadline is extended. A purchase of Imperial Brands would be the biggest deal among tobacco companies since British American Tobacco (BTI) bought Reynolds American for $60 billion in 2017.

Analysts Praise the Deal

Wall Street analysts were quick to praise a potential purchase of Imperial Brands by Altria. Stifel Financial (SF) said the acquisition would give Altria direct access to international markets, strengthen its smoke-free product portfolio and provide additional benefits from customs duty refunds. Stifel analyst Matthew Smith maintained a Buy rating and $82 price target on MO stock, which is 10% above current levels.

Citigroup (C) said the potential acquisition has "considerable strategic logic" as it would diversify Altria's traditional cigarette business and significantly expand its presence in next-generation tobacco and nicotine products. The firm does not anticipate any difficulties for Altria in financing the deal. Citigroup analyst Simon Hales has a Hold rating and $72 price target on MO stock.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Elon Musk Stands to Gain Over 70% Voting Power in a $3.5 Trillion SpaceX-Tesla Merger While Investors Lose Out
data.description:
A $3.5 trillion SpaceX-Tesla merger would hand Elon Musk over 70% voting power at the combined company. Regular investors are not likely to benefit on both sides of a deal. For example, SpaceX (SPCX) stockholders risk large earnings dilution in an all-stock buyout, while Tesla (TSLA) bulls could miss out on a lasting share rally.

Bloomberg reported on Nov. 12 that talks could bring a deal announcement as soon as December. Both boards set up special committees on Oct. 20, the Financial Times reported. Evercore (EVR) is advising three Tesla directors while Morgan Stanley (MS) and Goldman Sachs (GS) advise SpaceX's two-member panel.

Musk told Andrew Ross Sorkin at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Nov. 18 that both firms would probably be better off together. Tesla's Dec. 3 annual meeting in Austin omits a merger vote from its proxy ballot.

SpaceX's Profit Lead Could Create Dilution Risk in a Tesla Stock Swap

4-star RBC Capital Markets analyst Tom Narayan expects SpaceX to buy Tesla in a stock swap. "It's likely to happen," Narayan said, though timing depends on SpaceX's share price. SpaceX priced its record June IPO at $135 and bought xAI in February. Analysts project that SpaceX will generate more than $110 billion in 2027 EBITDA, more than six times Tesla's $18 billion estimate.

Tesla closed Wednesday at $380.14 and trades near 190 times estimated 2027 earnings, versus 32 times for SpaceX. At Narayan's $420-a-share value for Tesla, SpaceX would offer roughly three of its shares for each Tesla share. Tesla owners would hold about half of the combined group while bringing in just 15% of its profits.

"Tesla bulls banking on a SpaceX deal don't get the math," One World ETF co-founder Gary Black said. He pointed to Marvell's October all-stock buyout of Lumentum, which cut Marvell stock by 50% and left Lumentum down 35%.

Moreover, Wall Street views both shares differently. TipRanks data shows that SpaceX stock (SPCX) carries a Strong Buy rating, representing a whopping 108% upside potential. Meanwhile, Tesla stock (TSLA) holds a Moderate Buy rating and much lower upside potential at around 8%.

Dual-Class Stock Structure Hands Musk Majority Control

SpaceX's IPO prospectus gives Musk's Class B stock 10 votes per share against one vote for public Class A shares.This structure gives him roughly 82% of SpaceX's votes versus 20% at Tesla, and a combination would leave him above 70% voting control. Buying Tesla at a $2 trillion value would drop robot and operating targets from Musk's 2025 pay plan. He would collect about 35 million Tesla shares instead of up to 424 million. Any deal still requires "a 50% vote of all shares" outstanding at Tesla during a separate meeting, Musk said on SpaceX's Oct. 20 earnings call.

Terafab Chip Plant and China Regulators Shape Deal Timing

Cheaper custom chips sit behind the push to combine. SpaceX and Tesla are partnering with Intel (INTC) on a $16.8 billion Terafab chip plant in Grimes County, Texas. Narayan said $30,000 AI chips make humanoid robots "cost prohibitive" when raw production costs sit near $3,000 before Nvidia (NVDA) and TSMC (TSM) gross margins. Waiting for mid-2027 S&P 500 entry could lift SpaceX shares first, and Polymarket puts merger announcement odds at 86% by late 2027 versus 20% in 2026.

Bank of America analyst Alexander Perry also called Beijing the "main regulatory risk" for a deal. "A potential deal would place Tesla's Shanghai plant, which builds roughly half of its global vehicle output, under [SpaceX], a major U.S. defense contractor," Perry wrote.
data.author: Annika Masrani

data.title: U.S. Stock Market Rises on Strength in Tech Stocks
data.description:
U.S. stocks rose on Friday morning after the Thanksgiving holiday, driven by strength in technology stocks. The U.S. stock market will close today at 1 p.m. ET. Nasdaq Composite was up 0.59%, while the S&P 500 Index (SPX) and the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) were up 0.40% and 0.57%, respectively, as of 10:00 a.m. EST on November 27.

Major U.S. indexes remain on track to end the volatile week with strong gains. As of Wednesday's close, the S&P 500 was up nearly 4% for the week, while the Nasdaq Composite and Dow gained more than 4%. The week saw Nvidia (NVDA) stock surging more than 31% on Monday, as the chip giant's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO. However, Nvidia and other AI-related stocks gave back some of Monday's gains over the next two trading sessions.

Among trending stocks, SpaceX (SPCX) stock rose after Elon Musk announced his plans to donate an additional SPCX share to every child in the U.S. each year.

Altria (MO) stock trended lower after the tobacco giant confirmed that it was considering acquiring Imperial Brands (GB:IMB). The company said it was in discussions with a third party about a potential takeover of part of Imperial Brands' business.

Also, Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX) shares fell after the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) extended the review timeline for povetacicept, an experimental therapy for IgA nephropathy, a chronic kidney disease, by up to three months.

Oil futures were volatile this morning as traders assessed key developments in the Middle East, including attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy sites. At the time of writing, Brent crude futures, the international benchmark, fell 1.34% to $95.38 per barrel, while WTI crude futures rose 0.32% to $83.95 per barrel.
data.author: Sirisha Bhogaraju

data.title: Bitcoin (BTC) Has Hit Bottom, Says JPMorgan Chase
data.description:
JPMorgan Chase (JPM) has called a bottom in Bitcoin (BTC) after the largest cryptocurrency declined 20% over the past month. JPMorgan's chief cryptocurrency analyst, Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou, said that Bitcoin has likely reached "capitulation" after nearly two months of selling.

In a note to clients, Panigirtzoglou highlighted the record outflows from Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) during November, which are on track to top $5 billion, as a sign of a potential bottom. "The speed of the outflows has, if anything, been more intense than the outflows from early May to late June this year," he wrote.

The JPMorgan analyst added that retail investors likely drove much of the recent crypto ETF outflows and may have sold to buy stocks such as the newly public Anthropic (ANT).

The Strategy Factor

In addition to the ETF outflows, Panigirtzoglou cited an unconventional method to call a likely bottom in Bitcoin, with its price hovering near $60,000. The analyst cited a drop in Strategy's (MSTR) valuation relative to its Bitcoin holdings to a record low as a sign that capitulation has likely been reached.

Panigirtzoglou wrote that the ratio has fallen to around 0.88x, below the previous low seen in June of this year. The analysts' charts compare Strategy's enterprise value with the dollar value of its Bitcoin holdings, though the report does not specify the exact formula used.

Strategy's NAV Calculation

Strategy has its own way of calculating the ratio, which it calls mNAV. The company divides its common share price by the dollar value of its Bitcoin holdings per share. "The premium to NAV collapses to a new record low of 0.88 for MicroStrategy's stock, signaling capitulation in Bitcoin," wrote the analyst.

Bitcoin's price has fallen back to around $60,000 after recovering briefly from last week's two-year low of $56,000. Bitcoin was is rising in early trading on Nov. 27 and on track to end a seven-week losing streak that is its second-longest decline on record.
